concepts.title: India's Place in World Population
concepts.definition: India holds about 17 per cent of the world's population on a much smaller share of the world's land, making it one of the most populous countries; knowing who lives where, in what numbers and with what characteristics is the work of the census and population studies.
concepts.key_idea: One in every six humans is Indian: population size shapes every plan and resource.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees206.txt lines 103-130 (India 17 per cent of world population), 640-660 (share across states)
question_patterns: what share of the world's population lives in India
why is the study of population important for a country
what is a census and how often is it held in India
which states hold the largest share of India's population
how does India's population compare with the world's
calculate a population's percentage share from given numbers

solution_steps.action: divide the part by the whole
solution_steps.explain: The group's population over the world total gives the fraction.
Multiply by 100 to read the share in per cent.

concepts.title: What Determines Population Change: Births, Deaths and Migration
concepts.definition: Population size changes through three flows - births add people, deaths remove them, and migration shifts them across borders; the difference between birth rate and death rate gives natural growth, while healthcare, literacy and income steer all three flows.
concepts.key_idea: Births minus deaths is natural growth; migration adds the human shuffle on top.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees206.txt lines 312-440 (what determines the population of a country)
question_patterns: what are the causes of population change
define birth rate and death rate
how does migration change the population of a place
what is natural growth of population
how do healthcare and literacy affect population growth
find the natural growth when birth and death rates are given

solution_steps.action: take the difference of the rates
solution_steps.explain: Birth rate minus death rate is the natural growth rate.

concepts.title: Age Composition and the Working-Age Group
concepts.definition: A population is layered by age: around 27 per cent of Indians are below 15 years, nearly 65 per cent fall in the working-age group of 15 to 59, and the elderly share is rising fast - from about 14 per cent in 2023 toward 26 per cent by 2050 in ageing societies - a shift called population ageing.
concepts.key_idea: A young majority is a demographic dividend; a swelling elderly share is the coming challenge.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees206.txt lines 399-440 (ageing from 14 to 26 per cent), 967-975 (27 per cent under 15, 65 per cent working age)
question_patterns: what proportion of India's population is below 15 years
what is meant by the working-age population
explain population ageing with the 14 to 26 per cent projection
why is a large working-age group called a demographic dividend
what challenges does an ageing population bring
draw the age-group-wise distribution of India's population

solution_steps.explain: Split the population into children, working age and elderly.
Falling births and longer lives raise the elderly share year after year.
Jobs must absorb the young; pensions and healthcare must serve the old.

concepts.title: Sex Ratio, Literacy and Regional Patterns
concepts.definition: Population composition also tracks the sex ratio - women were about 48.5 per cent of the population in the most recent count - along with literacy rates that vary sharply among states, and uneven state-wise shares of population shaped by fertility, healthcare and development.
concepts.key_idea: Sex ratio and literacy map the quality of life across India's states.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees206.txt lines 440-530 (fertility and literacy rates), 640-660 (state shares), 741 (48.5 per cent women)
question_patterns: what is the sex ratio of India's population
compare the literacy rates of selected Indian states
why do some states have higher fertility rates than others
how is literacy linked to population growth
which states hold the largest shares of India's population
how does women's literacy influence family size

solution_steps.explain: Census tables give sex ratio, literacy and fertility by state.
Southern and western states generally show higher literacy and lower fertility.
Education, especially of women, lowers fertility and raises wellbeing.

worked_examples.question_pattern: India has {group_population} people out of a world population of {world_population}. Find India's percentage share.

solution_template.action: divide the country by the world
solution_template.explain: The fraction of humanity living in India.
Multiply by 100 for the share in per cent.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A country's birth rate is {birth_rate} per thousand and death rate is {death_rate} per thousand. Find its natural growth rate.

solution_template.action: subtract death rate from birth rate
solution_template.explain: Natural growth is the surplus of births over deaths.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A state has {group_population} people out of India's {world_population} people. Find the state's percentage share.

solution_template.action: divide the state by the nation
solution_template.explain: The state's fraction of the national total.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A place records a birth rate of {birth_rate} and a death rate of {death_rate} per thousand. How much did births exceed deaths?

solution_template.explain: The surplus of births over deaths drives natural growth.
